1. This is an application filed under Section 439 Cr.P.C, 1973 seeking grant of regular bail in FIR No.
443/2021dated 10.09.2021 under Section 304B/498A/34 IPC, 1860 registered at PS Baba Haridas Nagar, South-West Distrit Delhi filed on behalf of the accused.

2. The brief facts as mentioned in the Status Report are as under :-
"After the post mortem of the deceased Smt. Rekha, the viscera was preserved and dead body of deceased Smt. Rekha was handed over to Sh. Nirpat.
Subsequently above-mentioned case was registered.

sentences.text: All the above mentioned persons/witnesses levelled allegation against accused Radhey Shyam and their parents regarding demand of dowry from them and resulting mental and physical torture to deceased Smt. Rekha.

As per wedding Card Rekha got married to Radhey Shyam on 13 Dec 2015 as per Hindu Rituals"
3.

Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the applicant submits by referring to the FIR that so far as the demand of dowry is concerned, the complainant/mother of deceased has only said that there was a demand from the time of marriage for Rs.1,80,000/- and Rs.50,000/- and keeping in view the financial condition of the complainant, some times she gave Rs.2,000/- and sometimes Rs.3,000/-
from time to time to her deceased daughter.
That apart, learned counsel submits that there is no other allegation made against the applicant at all in the FIR.

4. Learned counsel refers to the Statement dated 28.09.2022 of the complainant/mother of the deceased/PW1 whereby the complainant had now changed her version contrary to what was rendered by her in the FIR and now submits that the applicant raised demands of dowry of Rs.
1,00,000/-, sometimes for Rs.80,000/- and sometimes for 50,000/-.

Learned counsel submits that the, complainant, apart from parroting the aforesaid demand, has not made any accusation or imputation that the said demands were made soon before the deceased committed suicide.
5. Learned counsel submits that the interpretation given to the words "soon before the death" is no more res integra.
Learned counsel submits that it need not be, remotely connected to the date and time of death.
According to learned counsel the demand of dowry has to have a causal connection to

According to the learned counsel, in the present case, neither there is any such statement given nor any evidence placed on record to show the connection between the incident and the alleged said demands of dowry.

6. That apart, learned counsel also brings attention of this Court to the Post Mortem Report enclosed with the Status Report, to submit that though the original allegations in the FIR are that the applicant was alleged to have placed Hot Chimta on the private parts of the deceased, however,
the same are belied by the fact the list of injuries in the post mortem report do not disclose any such injury on the deceased at all.
7. In fact, learned counsel submits that injuries according to the post mortem report, apart from the injuries on the neck which is ligature mark and etc.
are the classic injuries in case where person commit suicide, the other three injuries are on the lower portions of the leg which are usual to the persons who are working as a labourer in factories.

8. Learned counsel submits that the deceased was in fact working as a labourer in the factory and therefore the possibility of her having received such injuries during employment cannot be ruled Radhey Shyam Alias Babu vs State (Nct Of Delhi) on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11310205/

sentences.text: That apart, learned counsel also submits that the three primary witnesses i.e. the mother, the father and the brother of the deceased have already been examined, cross- examined and discharged.
He submits that only the formal witnesses are remaining to be examined.
9. That apart, learned counsel submits that the applicant has been incarcerated in judicial custody for almost 2 years.
There is no requirement for the applicant to be detained further.
10. Per-contra, Mr. Haider learned APP for the State reiterates the This is a digitally signed order.

1872 r/w Section 304B of IPC, 1860 has to be necessarily read against the applicant.
11.
Learned APP for the State also submits that the demands have detailed by the complainant/mother of the deceased and the remaining evidence shall be the subject matter of trial.
According to learned APP for the State, the evidence as of now, which is available on record is sufficient to disentitle the applicant from seeking regular bail.
12. Mr. Vishesh Wadhwa appears for the complainant and submits that the deceased was residing at her parental home 3 - 4 months prior to the date of incident.
Learned counsel submits that it is only after the deceased went back to her matrimonial home that the incident took place.
Learned counsel further submits that the incident having occurred immediately after she went back to the matrimonial home, gives the presumption which would be read against the applicant.
13. It is further stated by learned counsel that demand for dowry indeed was made and had continued over the years.

He further submits that there is no appropriate or simple definition to the words "soon before the death" and in that view, learned counsel submits that the said incident taking place immediately after the deceased went to her matrimonial home should be read against the applicant and he submits that the applicant does not deserve any bail.

14. This court has considered the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and Mr. Haider, learned APP for the State as well as Mr. Vishesh Wadhwa, learned counsel for the complainant.

The Nominal Roll dated 20.02.2023, which has been placed on record, indicates that the applicant was detained in judicial custody for a period of 1year, 4 months and 23 days barring an interim bail availed of in between, however, as of today, the incarceration would be almost 2 years.

sentences.text: Moreover, the jail conduct of the applicant has been recorded as satisfactory and no punishment has been issued to the applicant, in the meanwhile, by the jail authorities.

16. That apart, so far as the injuries are concerned, the post mortem report does not show any injuries on the private parts of the deceased and therefore, the version of the prosecution may not be completely correct though the same is subject matter of trial.

17. That apart, it is also not disputed that the public witnesses including PW1, PW2 & PW3 who are the mother, the father and the brother of the deceased are already examined, cross-examined and discharged, only formal witnesses are remaining to be examined.
18. It is apparent that the Trial court would further take some more time for conclusion of the proceedings.
19. This court is of the considered opinion that keeping in view the overall facts arising in the present case, the applicant is entitled to bail.
